scope: Thirty new production responsiveness/render-speed DSP costs removed after the merged prior 100. Startup, the prior 74 implemented findings, all round-two 100 findings, unused helpers and bug fixes are excluded.
runtimeClosure: Existing application DSP files only. No new desktop runtime inventory entries, assistance runtime source/pins/recipes/archives/targets, dependency pins or StaffPad native/WASM bytes changed.

parity.provenance: Independent esbuild bundle of /tmp/Soundscaper-perf-200-baseline captured before production edits, with all editor imports redirected to baseRevision; current helper executes the same scenarios against production sources.
parity.additionalAdversarialEvidence: Independent baseline/current bundles compared raw bytes across 1/31/511/512/513/2047/2048/2049/4097/8193-frame spectral and noise edges, arbitrary hop 7, maximal finite words, signed zero/subnormals, finite-overflow Paulstretch/Click Removal, sanitized NaN/Infinity Bitcrusher/Gate, irregular partitions and live parameter changes.
parity.ownership: All new scratch/geometry is invocation-local and synchronous. Returned PCM remains private. Queue producer chunks are copied before mutation/detachment; consumed chunks release. Workers, cancellation fences, source ownership and native StaffPad processing are unchanged.
parity.independentReviewEvidence: Independent timeline agent reran all 123 frozen hashes and 104 raw adversarial cases, then added 135 production partition/state/caller-PCM/queue-ownership comparisons. All matched exactly; review covered threshold rounding, Paulstretch ring/seed order, noise gains/geometry, FFT owned history overwrite, bounded Tremolo range, normalized gate updates, Vocoder envelope-only redesign and cubic/RNG mode/reset. No confirmed correctness, unused-path or old-ledger overlap issue across the thirty findings.

findings.title: Reuse one private Click Removal PCM window
findings.avoidedCost: Overlapping windows reuse one 8192-frame PCM buffer, clearing only uncopied tail frames.
findings.evidence: The 20113-frame stereo fixture allocates one scratch window instead of eight.
findings.limitations: Caller PCM is copied before the destructive window kernel; separation and write-back order remain unchanged.

findings.title: Reuse Click Removal detector squares, means and prefix scratch
findings.avoidedCost: One invocation-local workspace replaces three new Float64 buffers for each destructive window.
findings.evidence: The same fixture allocates three detector arrays instead of twenty-four.
findings.limitations: The public standalone kernel still allocates its own workspace when none is supplied; no cross-invocation cache.

findings.title: Prepare each Click Removal mean-power threshold once per window
findings.avoidedCost: Every width detector reuses the original threshold-times-mean/division result rather than recalculating it for each width.
findings.evidence: At maximumWidth 20, each of 4096 mean thresholds is calculated once instead of three times per window; PCM hashes retain exact arithmetic.
findings.limitations: Float64 mean rounding, threshold multiplication/division order, and width traversal stay unchanged.

findings.title: Share channel-independent Paulstretch overlap normalization
findings.avoidedCost: The identical output overlap weights are accumulated once per job instead of once per channel.
findings.evidence: Three-channel fixture now has one full-length normalization allocation rather than three.
findings.limitations: Every normalization sum retains its original window and tap order.

findings.title: Bound Paulstretch accumulation to the FFT window
findings.avoidedCost: Completed samples are emitted and their slots recycled, removing one output-length Float64 accumulation buffer per channel.
findings.evidence: The three-channel fixture has no full-length accumulation arrays; scratch is 256 frames per channel rather than 7105.
findings.limitations: Output PCM and one shared full-length normalization remain proportional to duration; seeded FFT/RNG and Float32 fade rounding are unchanged.

findings.title: Prepare Paulstretch input/output window bounds before sample loops
findings.avoidedCost: Valid intervals replace per-tap source/destination range branches, and only padded input edges are cleared.
findings.evidence: Six Paulstretch frozen fixtures plus huge-finite/edge differential cases preserve exact bytes.
findings.limitations: Interior samples are fully overwritten before FFT; no arithmetic reassociation.

findings.title: Write Noise Reduction residue into its rounded private output
findings.avoidedCost: Residue no longer allocates another complete PCM result after producing reduced audio.
findings.evidence: Two-channel residue output allocations fall from four to two.
findings.limitations: Reduced values still round to Float32 before original samples are subtracted.

findings.title: Share spectral-edit overlap normalization across channels
findings.avoidedCost: Gain/replacement compute their channel-independent denominator once instead of per channel.
findings.evidence: Selected-range Float64 normalization allocations fall from three to one in a three-channel fixture.
findings.limitations: Counted once across gain and replacement; exact sum order and untouched-time bytes are preserved.

findings.title: Reuse spectral-edit accumulation and FFT scratch between channels
findings.avoidedCost: Sequential channels reuse one accumulator and one/two transform pairs rather than allocate those arrays per channel.
findings.evidence: Three-channel gain uses two range-sized Float64 arrays and three window-sized arrays; replacement uses two and five.
findings.limitations: Invocation-local scratch is cleared/overwritten before reuse; returned channels remain independently owned.

findings.title: Bound spectral-edit sample loops and clear only padding
findings.avoidedCost: Prepared input/output intersections remove per-tap boundary checks and redundant full real-array clears.
findings.evidence: All 24 spectral gain/replacement hashes and arbitrary-hop/huge-finite edge cases remain byte-identical.
findings.limitations: One shared optimization across gain/replacement; imaginary spectra still clear fully before each forward FFT.

findings.title: Prepare Noise Reduction detector thresholds once for the selection
findings.avoidedCost: Sensitivity-times-profile power is constant per bin and shared across all time windows/channels.
findings.evidence: 1025 original products per channel-window become 1025 products per admitted job.
findings.limitations: Profile validation is retained; geometry is invocation-local so mutable profile changes in a later call cannot be stale.

findings.title: Store Noise Reduction frame gains in one contiguous buffer
findings.avoidedCost: One backing buffer replaces a new Float32 buffer and gain row for every analysis window.
findings.evidence: The 5099-frame stereo fixture reduces spectrum-sized Float32 allocations from 36 to 10; only five detector slots per channel remain.
findings.limitations: Every gain assignment retains Float32 rounding and original attack/release traversal order.

findings.title: Prepare Noise Reduction smoothing bin neighborhoods once
findings.avoidedCost: Clamped left/right smoothing neighborhoods are fixed per bin, removing repeated min/max and interval-width setup for every frame/channel.
findings.evidence: The 0/6/12-band smoothing hashes and padded-edge fixtures match exactly.
findings.limitations: Prefix-log and geometric-mean evaluation order remain unchanged; zero smoothing avoids allocating neighborhood arrays.

findings.title: Prepare Noise Reduction detector ring slots once per frame
findings.avoidedCost: The same neighboring spectrum positions serve all 1025 bins, avoiding repeated remainder arithmetic in every neighbor/bin comparison.
findings.evidence: At most five remainder operations per detector frame replace up to 5125; all profile/reduction hashes remain exact.
findings.limitations: Neighbor ordering and second-greatest tie behavior remain unchanged.

findings.title: Load bounded Noise Reduction/profile windows and clear only padding
findings.avoidedCost: A shared input loader overwrites valid taps and clears padded edges; resynthesis also iterates only valid output taps.
findings.evidence: Noise profile/reduction hashes and 1/31/511/512/513/2047/2048/2049-frame differential cases preserve exact bytes.
findings.limitations: Counted once across profile, detector and resynthesis; full imaginary clears remain required.

findings.title: Keep owned typed spectral queue chunks instead of boxed samples
findings.avoidedCost: Native PCM chunk copies avoid one JavaScript push/boxing per sample and periodic copying of retained audio samples. Consumed chunks release immediately.
findings.evidence: 4096-frame typed push visits zero JavaScript sample iterator entries instead of 4096; detached-buffer/double-precision/chunk-retirement tests pass.
findings.limitations: Producer scratch is copied synchronously before it can be mutated or detached; generic iterable values retain Array.from semantics.

findings.title: Omit unused Legacy peak-detector RMS history
findings.avoidedCost: Peak-only selections never use the100-frame RMS ring and no longer allocate/zero it.
findings.evidence: A3089-frame peak fixture allocates only its3089-frame Float64 envelope rather than an additional100-frame ring.
findings.limitations: RMS mode retains its original ring and sample arithmetic.

findings.title: Select Legacy output numerator before the PCM loop
findings.avoidedCost: The fixed detector choice no longer repeats the numerator branch for every emitted sample.
findings.evidence: Eight peak/RMS/normalization/ratio baseline hashes retain exact output.
findings.limitations: No division/exponent reassociation and no neutral-ratio shortcut; malformed direct inputs keep original calculations.

findings.title: Design linked loudness weighting coefficients once per job
findings.avoidedCost: Identical K-weighting coefficient design is shared across channels while histories stay private.
findings.evidence: Three-channel linked loudness tangent calls fall from six to two.
findings.limitations: Each channel still has separate shelf/high-pass state and original Float32 filter rounding.

findings.title: Skip unused first-order and neutral-shelf filter trigonometry
findings.avoidedCost: First-order filters need only tangent and neutral shelves need identity coefficients; sine/cosine are no longer evaluated before those returns.
findings.evidence: Three admitted first-order/neutral-shelf designs produce zero sine/cosine calls instead of three each.
findings.limitations: Parameter/Nyquist validation remains in the owning processor; other biquads retain original coefficient equations.

findings.title: Advance admitted Tremolo phase with a bounded wrap
findings.avoidedCost: Phase plus the bounded admitted frequency increment needs at most one subtraction rather than a floor every frame.
findings.evidence: 3089 output frames cause zero phase-floor calls; fifteen waveform/partition hashes remain exact.
findings.limitations: Reset still normalizes phase with floor. The previously slower indirect waveform dispatcher was reverted and is excluded.

findings.title: Reuse Noise Gate coefficients after equivalent normalized updates
findings.avoidedCost: Identical admitted controls preserve detector/crossover state without recomputing threshold, floor and release coefficients.
findings.evidence: Equivalent string/number update produces zero release exponentials; changed release produces one.
findings.limitations: Validation precedes reuse; raw merged parameters remain current so implicit lookahead defaults and later partial updates retain behavior.

findings.title: Retain the fixed Noise Gate attack normalization
findings.avoidedCost: The expm1(-1) attack denominator is shared instead of repeated for every opening sample/channel.
findings.evidence: An opening fixture evaluates the fixed denominator zero times after module initialization.
findings.limitations: Progress numerator and attack/hold/release state arithmetic are unchanged.

findings.title: Avoid constructing crossovers for fixed full-band selection gates
findings.avoidedCost: Fixed gateFrequency 0 jobs cannot change frequency and never use crossover history, so they omit two crossover objects and their arrays.
findings.evidence: Three-channel fixed full-band fixture allocates four Float64 detector arrays instead of eight.
findings.limitations: This is new allocation/design avoidance beyond the prior audit’s omitted tick/low work. Live gates retain crossover history for later frequency changes.

findings.title: Redesign only Vocoder envelopes when distance changes
findings.avoidedCost: Envelope distance leaves analysis/carrier/synthesis centers and oscillator rotations unchanged, so those filters/trigonometric rotations are retained.
findings.evidence: After independently preparing fixed Q values, a 12-band distance update uses 48 angular cosines instead of the full-bank 96. The separate fixed-Q saving is recorded by finding 26.
findings.limitations: Changed band count still redesigns/reset the full bank; envelope state is preserved as before.

findings.title: Prepare fixed Vocoder envelope pole Q values once
findings.avoidedCost: The four Butterworth Q values are identical for every band/update, avoiding repeated fixed-angle cosines.
findings.evidence: 12-band initialization uses96 angular cosines instead of144; Q values are computed four times at module initialization.
findings.limitations: No envelope/filter recurrence changes; independently owned biquad states remain private.

findings.title: Transform live EQ input directly into its retained spectrum slot
findings.avoidedCost: The next history slot is the FFT destination, removing two input-spectrum scratch arrays and two full-spectrum copies per partition.
findings.evidence: The 12817-frame stereo fixture removes 400 Float64 spectrum set calls.
findings.limitations: Only the oldest unneeded slot is overwritten; partition sum order and inverse rounding remain exact.

findings.title: Omit clearing live EQ input that the next partition overwrites
findings.avoidedCost: A full input partition rewrites every frame before processing, so its post-processing zero fill is redundant.
findings.evidence: The same stereo fixture removes 200 128-frame input fills.
findings.limitations: Partial partitions never FFT until complete; reset still replaces state with zeroed owned arrays.

findings.title: Skip unused Bitcrusher interpolation position geometry
findings.avoidedCost: Sample-hold and smooth reconstruction never read interpolation position and omit its division/clamp per frame.
findings.evidence: 3089 frames in each of two modes cause zero position Math.min calls instead of 6178.
findings.limitations: Held age, RNG advance, quantizer and smooth history continue unchanged for later mode updates.

findings.title: Share Bitcrusher cubic position basis across channels
findings.avoidedCost: Cubic powers and four position-only Hermite factors are calculated once per frame rather than once per reconstructed channel.
findings.evidence: Twenty dither/reconstruction/update hashes and partition/reset tests retain exact PCM; 8-channel basis calculations decrease eightfold.
findings.limitations: Channel tangents/mix and original polynomial evaluation order remain unchanged. Direct calls use local numeric arguments; slower indirect dispatcher forms were reverted. Warm whole-processor timing may be neutral.

isolatedMeasurements.method: Isolated warmed Node 26.5; 3 warmups and 9 paired trials, alternating which implementation runs first. Includes processor setup where named; excludes UI, I/O, Electron and startup. Concurrent development makes these diagnostic only.

clickLongSelection.name: click-4ch-480000
clickLongSelection.method: Four warmups and eleven alternating paired trials, same pure Node bundles; includes validation, copies and kernel processing, excludes UI/I/O/Electron.

isolatedMeasurements.interpretation: Diagnostic Node probes, not Electron workflow or timeline FPS evidence. Small Click Removal and cubic Bitcrusher warm medians may be neutral/slower despite reduced measured work; the long Click Removal allocation-intensive selection improves in this probe. No per-item universal latency gain is claimed. Rejected indirect Tremolo/Bitcrusher dispatcher implementations are absent from the final source/count.

cubicRecheck.name: bitcrusher-cubic-8ch-240000
cubicRecheck.method: Seven warmups and fifteen alternating paired trials using the same final direct-call implementation and independent baseline/current Node bundles; processor construction and output allocation included. Diagnostic only.
